articles.title: Google Photos users report handy drag-to-select feature has disappeared
articles.summary: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Google Photos users are reporting that a feature has suddenly gone missing. The affected users can no longer drag to select multiple photos. This problem has been spotted on Pixel, Galaxy, and OnePlus phones. Recently, Google Photos users have noticed that the app won’t let them search for terms related to regulated or illicit substances . While that appears to be an intentional choice implemented into Google’s guardrails, a new issue has popped up that seems unintentional. A convenient photo selection feature has suddenly disappeared from the app for some. Google Photos users are flocking to Reddit to report that drag to select no longer works for them. If you’re unfamiliar with drag to select, the feature allows you to select multiple photos

articles.title: Weekly poll results: smart glasses are a solution looking for a problem
articles.summary: Tech giants are spending tons of R&D money on building new smart glasses that fill various categories. However, based on the results from last week’s poll, all of them are solutions looking for a problem. The outcome couldn’t be more clear – the vast majority of voters are not using smart glasses. To be fair, regional availability is preventing some people from trying them out. But even then it’s clear that most people haven’t found a compelling use-case for them. articles.title: AI adoption isn’t the same as AI usage
articles.summary: Every engineering org I’ve talked to this year has some version of the same chart. Seat activations climbing. Token spend climbing. Somebody’s slide says 80% weekly active. Then you sit in that team’s planning meeting, and nothing about how they build software has changed. That gap is the actual problem, and most of the way we measure AI adoption is designed, accidentally, to hide it. Everything you’re measuring is a usage metric Token spend tells you someone typed into a box. Pull request count tells you commits landed. “Percentage of code written by AI” tells you an autocomplete got accepted. None of it tells you the work got better. Goodhart’s Law, right on schedule. articles.title: Hands-on: This modular controller slides open to transform your iPhone into a mobile game console [Video]
articles.summary: I first saw the Ohsnap MCON controller at CES last year, and I immediately fell in love with the concept. The idea was simple: give people a full-featured mobile controller that attaches to your phone via Magsafe, slides open when ready to use, and collapses into something compact that can go with you anywhere. Over the last two weeks, I have put it through its paces. I have tossed it around, pressed the launch mechanism 100s of times, used it with emulators, Apple Arcade games, and with multiple phones. Here is how it has held up, along with everything you need to know.

articles.title: Everyone thinks the iPhone Ultra will crush Samsung. They’re wrong
articles.summary: Apple won’t be able to waltz in and best the Galaxy Z Fold 8 by default. I understand the company’s track record and mass appeal, but the general consensus I’ve been seeing about Apple’s rumored iPhone Ultra assumes too much. I loved my hands-on time with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and I can’t wait to get my review unit. It’s a refreshing form factor. And given how much I still enjoy my original Pixel Fold , I don’t expect the novelty to wear off as some claim. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has made me more interested in the upcoming iPhone Ultra, but Apple has more work to do than people think. I know Apple is still formidable, but Samsung has a chance to hold its own with the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

articles.title: As a regular NotebookLM user, here are 5 things I want from Gemini Notebook
articles.summary: A few weeks ago, Google announced it was rebranding NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook . Initially, this change was purely cosmetic, but we’re already seeing signs that Google has big plans for the future. In fact, we’ve already seen a few new features like Collections , which finally lets you group related notebooks together like a playlist. That’s just the beginning, though, as a recent APK breakdown hints the tool may soon let users add website links as sources directly in the Gemini app, alongside a few other possible changes .

articles.title: The Motorola Razr Fold has an accessory problem that no one’s talking about
articles.summary: Foldable phones are fragile. That’s what a lot of people think, and while I don’t think foldables are as delicate as their reputation implies, you should protect a folding phone in the same way you would any other. I hate display scratches, even minor ones, so I always use a screen protector and a case with every phone I have. Then I got the Motorola Razr Fold , and that changed. Not because it’s a phone that doesn’t need screen protectors, but because it’s almost impossible to find quality accessories for the phone.

articles.title: The Pixel 10 Pro is a flawed and inconsistent phone — and I’m still using it one year later
articles.summary: I find it hard to believe that it’s been almost a year since I got my Pixel 10 Pro . Since August 28th, it has been my primary phone (almost) every day, and I adore this phone when it’s working as it should. The problem, as is often the case with Pixels, is that it doesn’t always work as Google intended. Looking back, it’s been a year of ups and downs with the Pixel 10 Pro, but it’s still the only phone I want to call my own.

articles.summary: It’s been more than two months since Google launched the Fitbit Air. While the $99 fitness tracker grabbed most of the attention, one of the biggest changes that arrived alongside it was Google replacing the Fitbit app with Google Health . At the time, Google said Health would become a unified platform for all of its health devices, including Fitbit trackers and Pixel Watches. AI was a major focus with features like the Health Coach, and the company also promised support for data syncing with multiple health platforms, including Apple Health .

articles.title: A Snapdragon-powered Pixel might sound amazing. Here’s why it’s a terrible idea
articles.summary: Credit: David Imel / Android Authority It’s been roughly five years since Google first dropped Snapdragon silicon in Pixel phones in favor of its Tensor processors. I think it’s fair to say this move has been a double-edged sword for the company. Sure, there’s been good everyday performance, capable on-device AI, and great camera capabilities. But the transition also brought modem issues, heating problems, and uncompetitive peak performance. This state of affairs has led enthusiasts to urge Google to return to Snapdragon silicon, and it seems like an intriguing idea at first. But the more I thought about this possibility, the more I realized this probably wouldn’t be a great move for Pixel phones.

articles.title: AI coding got faster. Why didn’t engineering?
articles.summary: AI is great at making individuals faster, but the surrounding systems are then slowing everything right back down. This result — or, rather, lack thereof — is amplified by company size and pull request size. To the point that, while AI investment has increased 28 times for most companies, and especially those with more than 99 engineers, velocity measures are stagnant and even down. Such is the finding of the recently released State of AI Impact in Engineering from DX, which measures engineering organizations across speed, effectiveness, quality, and impact . articles.title: Mount Toba eruption doesn't seem like it could nearly kill our species
articles.summary: Mount Toba was the biggest volcanic eruption in the last 2.6 million years, and some have suggested it nearly wiped out humanity. Park and his colleagues went looking for the records of that catastrophe in the mud taken from the bottom of a small crater lake on the Kenya-Tanzania border.
